content: Benfotiamine, also known as S-benzoylthiamine O-monophosphate, is a synthetic derivative of thiamine (vitamin B1) that belongs to the S-acyl group of compounds. It has been approved for medical use in Germany since 1993 under the trade name Milgamma. In Germany, it is prescribed for the treatment of sciatica and other painful nerve conditions. Additionally, combinations of benfotiamine with pyridoxine (vitamin B6) or cyanocobalamin (vitamin B12) are also marketed under the same trade name. Depending on the regulatory authority, benfotiamine is sold either as a medicine or as a dietary supplement. Benfotiamine is primarily marketed as an antioxidant dietary supplement. In a clinical study involving six patients, benfotiamine was shown to reduce advanced glycation end products (AGEs) by 40%. It is believed to have potential therapeutic applications in the treatment of diabetic retinopathy, neuropathy, and nephropathy. However, most of the effects attributed to benfotiamine are based on findings from in vitro and animal studies. Unfortunately, there is a lack of robust evidence from human studies, particularly endpoint studies. Therefore, additional clinical trials are necessary to fully explore the therapeutic potential of benfotiamine in both diabetic and non-diabetic pathological conditions. The proposed mechanism of action for benfotiamine involves increasing intracellular levels of thiamine diphosphate, which serves as a cofactor for the enzyme transketolase. This enzyme plays a critical role in redirecting substrates of advanced glycation end products (AGEs) and advanced lipoxidation end products (ALEs) into the pentose phosphate pathway, thereby reducing tissue accumulation of AGEs. Pharmacologically, after absorption, benfotiamine can be dephosphorylated by cells expressing ecto-alkaline phosphatase, converting it into the lipid-soluble compound S-benzoylthiamine. It is important to note that benfotiamine should not be confused with allithiamine, a naturally occurring thiamine disulfide derivative with a distinct pharmacological profile.
